list.name: device
list.label: Device
list.query: SHOW TAG VALUES FROM "pebble_minute" WITH KEY = "device"

panels.title: Raw points — no GROUP BY, no aggregation
vmc, raw (collapsed/overwritten points would show as a flat gap here)
panels.description: One point per stored minute, plotted individually with no time bucketing. A real backfill should show a dense, continuous scatter of points across the whole selected range; a stall or timestamp collision shows up as a cluster followed by an empty gap.

panels.title: Last 500 raw pebble_minute rows
panels.description: Exact stored timestamps, newest first. Look for: repeated identical Time values (would mean writes are colliding), a Time column that jumps straight from now to many days ago (would mean the backfill only ever completes one page), or Time values that don't fall on :00 seconds (would mean the minute-snap isn't happening).

targets.query: SELECT "steps", "hr", "vmc", "orientation", "light" FROM "pebble_minute" WHERE "device" =~ /^$device$/ AND $timeFilter ORDER BY time DESC LIMIT 500

panels.title: Points received per hour
panels.description: Should be ~60 per hour while worn. A backfill that's stuck after the first page shows as a single tall bar followed by nothing; normal catch-up shows a steady climb toward 60/hr; real gaps (watch off wrist, phone unreachable) show as legitimate dips to 0.

targets.query: SELECT count("vmc") FROM "pebble_minute" WHERE "device" =~ /^$device$/ AND $timeFilter GROUP BY time(1h) fill(0)

panels.title: Distinct minute-points stored (selected range)
panels.description: If this is suspiciously low relative to the time range (e.g. 1-20 instead of thousands over 7 days), points are colliding on write or the backfill is stalling, not a Grafana display artifact.

targets.query: SELECT * FROM "pebble_daily" WHERE "device" =~ /^$device$/ AND $timeFilter ORDER BY time DESC LIMIT 50
SELECT * FROM "pebble_activity" WHERE "device" =~ /^$device$/ AND $timeFilter ORDER BY time DESC LIMIT 50
